text:
The story with Mason Lohrei is not on the ice right now; it's the press box. Boston coach Marco Sturm scratched him again in mid-November, and 98.5 The Sports Hub's headline on Nov. 17 said Lohrei "doesn't seem to be on board with latest benching." He's played 20 games and sat out the 6-2 loss to Minnesota.

The numbers explain the coach's side. With Lohrei on the ice at five on five, Boston gets 46% of shot attempts and expected goals, almost 11 points worse than when he sits. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, with opponents getting more chances with him out there than against almost any other defenseman (bottom 4%).

The case for him is the puck. He's 6-foot-5, has 3 goals and 6 points in 17.9 minutes a night, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving the zone with possession on 56% of exits last season. He's 25, a 2020 second-round pick who has played 211 games for Boston. How Sturm uses him from here says a lot about whether the Bruins see him as part of the core.
